Built a File Management Utility in Python (Tkinter for the GUI). The app lets you browse folders and search by name or extension. You can sort by any column and create, rename, copy, move and delete files and folders. A Folder Summary shows file counts, total size and a breakdown by file type, and an "Organize by Type" feature sorts a messy folder into Images, Documents, Audio, Video, Archives, Code and Other sub-folders.

Input validation checks every name and path before anything on disk is touched. It rejects empty or over-long names, illegal characters, reserved system names and non-existent paths. It also blocks copying or moving a folder into itself and protects drive roots from being modified. Custom exceptions separate bad input (ValidationError) from failed operations (FileOperationError), so the GUI shows a clear message instead of crashing. Nothing is ever overwritten silently, and if one file fails during Organize, the rest are still processed and the failures are reported.

The project is split into modules: gui.py (interface), file_operations.py (all disk operations), file_processor.py (data processing: size formatting, categorizing, summaries, search, sort, organize planning), validators.py (input validation) and exceptions.py (custom errors). I included a unittest suite of 42 tests that run inside temporary folders so no real files are touched. I also tested the GUI end to end on a virtual display, and the README documents the workflow and design decisions.
